lit.\u0027\u003cdiv class=\"card-kicker\"\u0:
"
Hill equation with CO competition
"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCada metal cumple un:
"

Each metal plays a role according to its chemistry: Zn²⁺ as a Lewis acid (carbonic anhydrase), Mg²⁺ in chlorophyll, Cu in electron-transfer proteins (azurin) and hexacoordinate Fe in cytochromes. Toxic metals act by substitution (Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺) or by soft affinity for –SH (Hg²⁺); chelators (EDTA, BAL) remove them from the blood.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eCO\u0:
"

CO is a π-acceptor ligand that binds Fe²⁺ with an affinity ≈ 210 times greater than O₂ and leaves Hb in the R form, which retains the remaining O₂: the blood carries less oxygen and delivers it poorly. Increase pCO and watch the O₂ saturation fall.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003ehe:
"

In hemoglobin and myoglobin, Fe²⁺ is bound to the 4 N of a porphyrin and to the proximal histidine; the sixth position is left free for O₂. In the deoxygenated form, the Fe (high spin) sticks out ~0.4 Å from the plane; on binding O₂ (low spin) it moves into the plane and pulls the histidine along, which triggers the change in protein structure.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa hemoglobina tiene:
"

Hemoglobin has 4 subunits and binds O₂ cooperatively: each bound O₂ makes the next easier, and the curve is sigmoidal (Hill n ≈ 2.8, P₅₀ ≈ 26 mmHg). Myoglobin, with a single subunit, is hyperbolic (P₅₀ ≈ 2.8 mmHg). This way Hb loads O₂ in the lungs and unloads it in the tissues.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003epH má:
"

A lower pH (more CO₂ and H⁺ in active tissues) stabilizes the deoxygenated form and shifts the curve to the right: P₅₀ rises and Hb delivers more O₂ right where it is needed (Bohr effect). Here P₅₀ = 26·100.45(7.4 − pH), a simplified model.

"
